C: C1 [ C ] a piece of thin material worn by women to cover the face or head
› A Christian woman who takes the veil becomes a nun.
› A Muslim woman who takes or adopts the veil decides to wear traditional Muslim clothing.
決定穿戴穆斯林女性的傳統服裝

S: › [ S ] literary a thin covering that hides something or stops you from seeing something clearly
C2 [ S ] literary something that prevents you from knowing what is happening
› to not talk any more about a subject because it could cause trouble or embarrassment

T often passive: › [ T often passive ] to cover something, especially the face or body, with a veil
用幕遮掩；（尤指）用面紗遮住

T: › [ T ] to hide or cover something so that you cannot see it clearly or understand it

example: After the ceremony, the bride lifted up her veil to kiss her husband.
儀式過後，新娘撩起面紗親吻她的丈夫。
The women wore black veils that covered all but their eyes.
那些女人戴著黑色面紗，把除眼睛之外的所有地方都遮住了。
The view over the lake was obscured by a veil of mist that hung in the air.
薄霧籠罩下，湖面上的景色看上去模模糊糊的。
We want to lift the veil of secrecy that surrounds government decisions.
我們想要揭開有關政府決策的神秘面紗。
I think we should draw a veil over everything that happened at the party, don't you?
我覺得我們不應再提派對上發生的任何事，不是嗎？
In some societies, women are expected to be veiled when they go out in public.
在某些社會裡，女性去公共場合就得戴上面紗。
Thick fog veiled the city.
濃霧籠罩著城市。

NONE: › Veiled words or ways of behaving are not direct or expressed clearly.
不明言的；含蓄的；掩飾的

example: a veiled reference/threat/warning
含蓄的指稱／威脅／警告
a thinly veiled attack on his abilities as a leader
對他的領導能力幾乎不加掩飾的攻擊

C: C1 [ C ] a tube that carries blood to the heart from the other parts of the body
› [ C ] the frame of a leaf or an insect's wing
› [ C ] a narrow layer of a substance that forms in or fills a crack in rock

S: › [ S ] a particular quality or characteristic

S or U: › [ S or U ] a style or a temporary mood

example: A rich vein of iron ore was found in the hillside.
山坡上發現了儲量豐富的鐵礦礦脈。
A vein of satirical anger runs through all his work.
在他的所有作品中，字裡行間都充滿了嬉笑怒罵。
In its bid to be elected, the party is attempting to tap (= use) an underlying vein of nationalism in the country.
該黨正試圖利用國內潛在的民族主義傾向來競選上臺。
The opening scene is very violent, and the rest of the movie continues in (a) similar vein.
影片一開場就充滿暴力，而其餘部分也是類似風格。
After laughing about the photograph, they began to talk in (a) more serious vein about the damaging effect it could have on his career.
他們笑過那張照片之後，開始認真談論它可能會對他的事業造成的破壞性影響。

NONE: › with many veins, or covered with lines that look like veins
有靜脈（或葉脈、翅脈）的；有紋理的

example: A thin, veined hand lay on the coverlet.
一條青筋暴起、乾癟消瘦的手搭在床罩上 。
